title: Event mesh validator and backpressure shepherd for usage signals
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Usage events submitted from the Console (route-level dashboards, API calls, and SDK clients) show intermittent downstream fanout drops when downstream sinks (billing, metrics, retention store) lag or fail. Current ingestion job rejects on strict schema mismatch and uses a coarse global rate limit that either throttles good traffic or lets malformed payloads skip further validation. We need an event mesh component that validates schemas early, routes events to multiple sinks with schema-aware fanout, and applies graceful backpressure and targeted rate-shedding so high-priority signals (billing, SLA metrics) keep flowing while lower-priority telemetry is selectively delayed or shed.
acceptance_criteria: New 'event-mesh' service validates incoming usage events against the canonical schema registry and rejects only when a defined critical contract (billing fields, customer_id, timestamp) is missing.
Event mesh can fan out a single validated message to three sinks concurrently (billing, metrics, retention) and apply per-sink routing rules configured via dynamic policy.

Backpressure policy supports: (a) circuit-open on repeated sink failures, (b) per-sink queue depth signaling to upstream, and (c) dynamic shedding that drops non-critical fields or lower-priority events based on knobbed thresholds.
Metrics and tracing added: per-schema validation latency, per-sink enqueue time, dropped-event counters broken down by reason, and a derived SLA metric that estimates billable-event delivery rate.
Service exposes an admin endpoint to replay N days of held events for a given customer and to toggle per-customer priority for shedding behavior.

Automated e2e test harness simulates sink slowdowns and verifies that billing events maintain >=99.5% delivery within target window while lower-priority telemetry can be shed to keep cost and latency SLOs.
tasks: Design: document event-mesh architecture and failure modes (contrib: Marco Diaz) - PRD link provided in links
Implement schema validation module using canonical registry client - use compiled JSON schema and typed transformers
Implement fanout worker with per-sink adapter interface and retry/backoff policies
Implement backpressure controller: queue depth monitor, sink health probes, and shedding policy engine
Add observability: Prometheus metrics, structured traces, and a Grafana dashboard prototype
Integration tests: consumer simulation harness that injects variable latency/HTTP 5xx patterns
Add admin endpoints for replay and per-customer priority toggles; wire with Console RBAC
Performance run: benchmark 95th p99 p999 latencies on representative sample workload and tune batching parameters
